alex (customer): Hey, we started getting 429s from mobile users this morning. App uses a single API key for org X, low QPS (~2 rps total), not hitting project limits. Any idea why?

sasha (support): Sorry about that — can you paste one raw request + the full response headers (curl -v output is best)? Also are you behind a CDN/proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For?

alex (customer): Yep behind a CDN. Here's a trimmed curl we ran with -v (token redacted):

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Org-ID: org_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

Response headers we got (trimmed):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 4
X-Redwood-Quota-Scope: ip
X-Request-ID: req_01F8XYZ
```

sasha (support): Thanks — that X-Redwood-Quota-Scope: ip is interesting. Can you confirm the CDN is forwarding client IPs (X-Forwarded-For) or NATting to a pool? Also, any chance multiple projects share the same key?

alex (customer): CDN does pass X-Forwarded-For (we see client IPs) but they also NAT egress in the same region (so many requests end up from same egress IP). We use one API key per product line, only one project linked to the key.

miguel (sre): Looking at logs for req_01F8XYZ — attribution fields: org_id=org_abc123, project_id=null, api_key_id=key_zzz, nat_ip=34.201.12.45. Quota decision picked scope=ip due to legacy heuristic that picks IP when X-Forwarded-For header present. Repro steps: send 50 quick requests behind same egress IP -> hits ip-scoped quota despite key managers.

miguel (sre): Short explanation: our rate-scope code currently prefers detectible client IP over api_key when X-Forwarded-For is present and api_key is from a multi-tenant org. That causes shared egress to aggregate and exhaust ip-based buckets.

alex (customer): Oof. That explains it. Is there a workaround we can do on our side while you patch?

sasha (support): Two short-term options: 1) Create a dedicated API key that we map to a project-level quota (we can set a higher project limit) — low friction. 2) Ask your CDN to preserve a private header like X-Orig-Client or stop rewriting X-Forwarded-For so we attribute to API key. Option 1 is fastest.

miguel (sre): We're opening ENG-4521 to change scoping precedence to prefer authenticated api_key/project over IP when api_key is present. Canary deploy planned in ~3h, full rollout after validation. Ticket: ENG-4521.

deploy-bot: canary deploy ENG-4521 scheduled to infra-canary cluster at 2026-03-17T14:30Z.

sasha (support): I've created a temporary project-level quota bump for org_abc123 (ID: Q-20260317-12) to reduce immediate 429s. If you can rotate/create the dedicated key I mentioned we can bind it to a project and avoid IP attribution.

alex (customer): Thanks — we'll generate a new key and test. Appreciate the quick triage.

miguel (sre): One more note: billing/usage will be attributed to whichever scope handled the request at the time (so some calls may record against ip buckets). If you'd like retro attribution adjustments, PM support and we'll review high-level totals.

alex (customer): Got it — will follow up if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
